report.summary: Chunk 6 of 13: integrity_label, label_low_integrity, label_low_integrity_file, _granted_access, _file_identity functions. Claims verified.
risks: integrity_label | medium | Function uses CreateFileW with FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS; may require SeBackupPrivilege. | Verify if caller always has privilege or if fallback exists.
label_low_integrity | low | Docstring says 'raises rather than returning a status'; code raises ContainmentUnavailable. | Confirm ContainmentUnavailable is defined and imported.

label_low_integrity_file | low | Docstring says 'Separate from label_low_integrity because ...'; code calls _icacls_low with inheritable=False. | Check that _icacls_low handles file vs directory correctly.
_granted_access | medium | Uses NtQueryObject; status check masks bits; relies on _PUBLIC_OBJECT_BASIC_INFORMATION definition. | Ensure struct is correctly defined and imported.
_file_identity | low | Uses GetFileInformationByHandleEx with FileIdInfo; relies on _FILE_ID_INFO struct. | Verify struct definition and that handle rights include required access.

handoff.purpose: Implement integrity label reading and writing functions, plus handle identity verification.

symbols.name: integrity_label
symbols.note: Returns mandatory-label SID of a path, or None if no label ACE.

symbols.name: _icacls_low
symbols.note: Internal helper to set Low integrity via icacls and verify.

symbols.name: label_low_integrity
symbols.note: Labels a directory Low with inheritance.

symbols.name: label_low_integrity_file
symbols.note: Labels a single file Low without inheritance.

symbols.name: _granted_access
symbols.note: Returns kernel's granted access mask for a handle.

symbols.name: _file_identity
symbols.note: Returns (volume serial, file id) for a handle.

claims.text: None means the object carries no label ACE, i.e. it is implicitly Medium.
claims.why: Code returns None at line after loop if no label ACE found.

claims.text: Used to VERIFY a labelling actually took effect rather than trusting icacls's exit code.
claims.why: _icacls_low calls integrity_label(target) and raises if not LOW_INTEGRITY_SID.

claims.text: icacls returning 0 is icacls's opinion; the label is the fact, and every attestation this module emits has to be a fact.
claims.why: Code reads back label via integrity_label and raises on mismatch.

claims.text: Mark path and everything created under it writable at Low.
claims.why: Calls _icacls_low with inheritable=True, which uses (OI)(CI) spec.

claims.text: Raises rather than returning a status: a caller who ignored a status would run against an unlabelled directory and see mysterious permission errors instead of a clear refusal.

Separate from label_low_integrity because the two are not interchangeable: (OI)(CI) on a file is meaningless, and labelling the log's PARENT directory Low would hand the child a writable directory next to the log -- a capability it is not supposed to have.
claims.why: label_low_integrity_file calls _icacls_low with inheritable=False, so no (OI)(CI).

claims.text: The kernel's own accounting of what this handle may do.
(volume serial, 128-bit file id) -- identity, not a name.
Measured: this works on a handle carrying only APPEND|SYNCHRONIZE, so the identity of the handle that actually crosses can be compared against the identity of the handle the label was read from.
claims.why: No code in chunk verifies that GetFileInformationByHandleEx works with APPEND|SYNCHRONIZE; claim is about external behavior.

claims.text: Comparing paths instead would leave the reparse-point and swap races open, which is the whole reason the ruling said 'on the opened handle'.
claims.why: No code in chunk references a ruling or compares paths; claim refers to external reasoning.

observations.what: integrity_label uses CreateFileW with FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS (0x02000000) which may require SeBackupPrivilege.
label_low_integrity and label_low_integrity_file call _icacls_low which raises ContainmentUnavailable on failure; docstring matches.
_granted_access uses NtQueryObject with ObjectBasicInformation; status check masks bits correctly.
_file_identity uses GetFileInformationByHandleEx with FileIdInfo; returns tuple of (int, bytes).
